text:
Mike Thompson addresses military strain and agricultural threats in recent statements
J. J. Rice
Rep. Mike Thompson, a U.S. Congressman representing California’s 4th district since 1999, addressed several issues affecting his constituents and the nation in a series of posts on social media this week.
On August 18, Thompson highlighted the ongoing challenges faced by the crew of a deployed naval vessel: "The USS Abraham Lincoln and her crew have been deployed long past their original return date under constant combat conditions with limited port calls, putting considerable strain on the sailors. They are low on food and toiletries, morale is terrible, toilets are clogged, and https://t.co/bJXrwY9o5b".
The following day, Thompson acknowledged federal action on an environmental issue involving waterfowl conservation. On August 19 he wrote, "Glad the U.S. Department of the Interior listened to the over 200,000 commenters, including myself, who submitted feedback on this proposed rule. They reversed course on a dangerous proposal that could have drained large portions of North America’s most critical waterfowl".
Later that same day, Thompson turned attention to agricultural threats facing California's wine industry. In a post thanking local media coverage dated August 19 he stated, "Thank you, @spectrumnewsca, for covering the Glassy-Winged Sharpshooter issue that could cost our winemaking community $104 million annually if this pest is not contained. I have been leading the fight in ensuring our winemaking community receives the support it needs to address".
Thompson was born in St Helena, California in 1951 and continues to reside there at age 72. He earned his BA from California State University, Chico in 1982.
